name: Bob James
hook: A CTI Records jazz-funk keyboardist whose orchestral instrumentals, drum breaks and bells became some of the most sampled recordings in hip-hop.
blurb: Bob James was discovered by Quincy Jones in 1963 and later became a producer and arranger for Creed Taylor's CTI Records, where his own 1970s albums blended jazz with funk rhythm sections and orchestral arrangements, made for a jazz-fusion audience. A decade later they became raw material for hip-hop drum breaks and hooks, a crossing this map comes back to often. His 1975 track 'Take Me to the Mardi Gras' became famous for its ringing bells, sampled by Run-D.M.C. on 'Peter Piper' (1986), and his 1974 track 'Nautilus' has been sampled in dozens of hip-hop records since. Sample-database sites credit each of the two with dozens of hip-hop uses, among the most of any recordings.
